title: Clauses watchlist — annotated margin notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal margin notes for fast triage during calls / redlines. Keep this as a live scratch doc — pragmatic asks, prioritized escalation triggers, and a few stock phrasings to drop into replies. Not polished; meant for use in real-time with Sales/AE and Solutions on calls.

Top-level negotiation priorities (short):
- Keep IP ownership clean (we want customer data + improvements use to be narrowly scoped).
- Limit data access/use to serve + improve our service only (no broad research/derivative rights).
- Liability cap and carveouts — try to get non-monetary carveouts removed or narrowed.
- Termination/transition: ensure data return/secure delete and transition assistance obligations are explicit.
- SLA and credits: clearly measurable and capped. Avoid open-ended remedies.

Risk tiers (for triage):
- High risk (escalate to Legal immediately): broad data license, unlimited indemnities, indefinite audit rights, vendor-hosted backups w/o controls, export-control clause that conflicts with our ops.
- Medium risk (discuss with AE + Solutions, then Legal as needed): insurance mismatch, vague ‘reasonable efforts’ security language, subcontractor blanket consent, ambiguous IP improvement rights.
- Low risk (handle locally): standard confidentiality language tweaks, request for minor time extensions, routine warranty cleanups.

Clause-by-clause margin notes (short-form):
1) Data use / License to use customer data
   - Risk: High if language grants perpetual rights or rights to use derivatives for any purpose.
   - Negotiation objective: Limit to (a) provide the service, (b) improve the service (internal model tuning) with anonymization or opt-out, (c) not sell to third parties.
   - Suggested ask: "Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, limited license to process Customer Data solely to provide and improve the Services; Provider will not sell Customer Data or derived outputs to third parties."
   - Fallback: Add time-limited research exception (e.g., 2 years) + opt-out for regulated customers.
   - Redline hint: strike "worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free, irrevocable" for broad research rights.

2) IP ownership & improvements
   - Risk: Vendor claiming ownership of model weights or embeddings created from customer data.
   - Objective: Customer retains ownership of their data and outputs; Provider owns platform improvements but not customer-specific outputs.
   - Suggested language: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Output. Provider retains ownership of pre-existing technology and platform improvements not derived from Customer Data."
   - Notes: If customer wants improvements assigned away, consider co-existence language or license-back.

3) Liability cap & exclusions
   - Risk: Unlimited liability or broad carveouts that eliminate the cap.
   - Objective: Keep cap = greater of (X * annual fees) or reasonable flat limit; carveouts limited to willful misconduct/fraud only.
   - Suggested ask: "Aggregate liability capped at the greater of $5M or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months. Carveouts limited to gross negligence and willful misconduct; not for ordinary breaches."
   - Escalate if counterparty insists on no cap for indirect commercial losses.

4) Indemnity
   - Risk: Broad indemnity covering customer IP, end-user claims, or third-party claims tied to customer's use.
   - Objective: Narrow indemnity to IP infringement claims caused by Provider’s software; exclude customer misuse and data breaches unless caused by Provider’s gross negligence.
   - Suggested redline: Limit to "claims that Provider's unmodified Services infringe a third party's IP."

5) Security & breach notification
   - Risk: Vague obligations and long notification windows.
   - Objective: Commit to industry-standard controls (SOC/ISO where applicable), 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, cooperation language for remediation.
   - Ask: "Provider will notify Customer of confirmed data breaches within 72 hours and provide remediation plan."

6) Audit & compliance rights
   - Risk: Unlimited audit frequency or physical audits at short notice.
   - Objective: Accept periodic audits (once/year or via third-party attestation) and reasonable notice; restrict to scope for Customer Data only.
   - Fallback: Provide SOC2 reports and remote-only audit rights unless specific high-risk customer requests otherwise.

7) Data residency & export controls
   - Risk: Contract requires data to be stored in customer region but Provider uses multi-region infra; OR contract restricts transfers in ways incompatible with cloud infra.
   - Objective: Provide region guarantee for PII/regulatory data; include allowed exceptions (disaster recovery) and require encryption.
   - Note to self: If customer is EU regulated, propose EU-region only + SCCs; escalate for APAC legal requirements.

8) Termination & transition assistance
   - Risk: No defined exit support or transfer windows, or overly short return/erase periods.
   - Objective: 90 days export window, transition assistance at reasonable rates or included for certain scenarios (termination for convenience vs breach).
   - Suggested: "Upon termination, Provider will make Customer Data available for 90 days in a common format and certify secure deletion within 30 days after data retrieval."

9) SLA / Performance credits
   - Risk: Vague uptime SLOs with uncapped remedies.
   - Objective: Measurable SLOs with credits capped (e.g., credits limited to % of monthly fees). Avoid service termination for single outage unless gross pattern.

10) Subcontractors & resale
   - Risk: Blanket consent to subcontractors with no notice.
   - Objective: Require Provider to list major subprocessors and provide notice for changes; allow escalation for critical subprocessors (e.g., model hosting).

Negotiation playbook (live):
- Opening posture: Start conservative on IP/data; give commercial concessions (discounts, term) in exchange for stricter data/IP language.
- Leverage points: SLAs (we can offer credits not termination), Dedicated/Private deployment as premium to unblock data residency asks, reporting/attestation in lieu of audits.
- Sequence: 1) Triage high-risk clauses in first pass (data/IP/liability), 2) Agree on security attestations, 3) Flow through remaining commercial points.
- On calls: Keep template language ready; read back the ask and the business rationale.

Stock phrasings to paste into emails/replies:
- "Can you confirm that the license to use Customer Data is limited solely to providing and improving the Services and that Provider will not sell Customer Data or derived outputs?"
- "We need a liability cap that is proportional to fees — propose the greater of $5M or 2x fees paid in prior 12 months."
- "For audit requests, we can provide SOC2 reports and accommodate a remote compliance review annually; on-site audits require 30 days' notice and are limited in scope."

Escalation triggers (when to pull Legal ops):
- Counterparty refuses any cap or carves out everything from the cap.
- Broad data license that allows sale/redistribution of Customer Data or model weights.
- Indemnity covering customer downstream claims.
- Data residency ask that requires custom infra/region commitment from us.

Notes to self / negotiation memory log (use after calls):
- Record the exact problematic sentence and propose discrete substitutes.
- If Sales agrees to commercial trade (discount, PO term, larger deal) capture in thread — legal needs the commercial quid pro quo.
- Keep a short list of customers with special clauses (e.g., EU-regulated, healthcare) -> reuse earlier precedents.

Quick references (placeholders to replace with real links during negotiation):
- Confluence: Legal redline playbook (internal) — CONFLUENCE-LEGAL-12345
- Jira: Track negotiated exceptions — LEGAL-4821
- Slack thread: #terms-negotiation-thread (pinned examples)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm acceptable numeric caps with Leadership (A: suggest $5M/2x fees vs B: team prefers $10M floor).
- Build a quick one-pager for Solutions on how to position Private/Dedicated as a solution for data residency asks.
- Add standard sample language for model-tuning opt-out for regulated customers.

Final quick checklist before sending counterparty redline:
- Have we limited data use to service+improve (no sale)?
- Is IP ownership preserved for customer outputs?
- Is liability cap present and reasonable?
- Are indemnities appropriately narrow?
- Are security attestations included (SOC2 or equivalent)?

"Be pragmatic — get the deal live with guardrails. If it's a strategic customer, accept reasonable operational commitments but document them and set clear expiration/roll-off points."

-- end of scratchpad --
